messages:
carla: Heads-up — canary showing a spike in token billing when clients do aggressive reconnects after keepalive drops. Seems like each reconnect is billed as a new session instead of resume.
ben: Ugh. Is that the case where client gets a 204 from the proxy and immediately reconnects?
alice: Possibly. If resume token is absent we treat as fresh request. Do we know why resume token is missing?
carla: Logs show client sometimes drops resume-id header (X-Resume-Id) on the reconnect path. But even when resume-id present, downstream billing shows two start events: `connect_method=new` and then `connect_method=resume` a few ms later.
ben: That smells like double-counting in the router: route switch emits a start-monotonic event for the new socket, then resume path reconciles but billing metric already incremented.
dan: From product side — customers will notice cost spikes. We need a short-term console annotation so we don't get paged for noise. Also need a rollout flag to throttle aggressive reconnects rather than forcing a hard change.
alice: Technical detail: our meter counts per-session token windows. When session object created by gateway, meter increments. If we create a transient session to accept the first SYN then immediately PATCH it to resume, the meter doesn't retract.
carla: Repro steps I ran: curl SSE connect -> proxy returns 204 keepalive -> client re-open with resume-id -> console shows 2 starts for same trace id. Paste logs: ```
[proxy] accept socket id=abc123 trace=tr-9 start_event=true
[router] route switch to runtime-2 start_event=true
[auth] resume token validated for trace=tr-9
[router] reconciled resume for socket id=abc123 start_event=false (should retract?)
```
ben: We don't have a 'retract' path in metering. Metering is intentionally append-only for safety; but we can emit a reconciliation tag that the billing pipeline understands and prevents double-charge.
alice: Agree. Two options: (A) change router to avoid emitting start until resume validated; (B) emit reconciliation events so billing dedupes. (A) safer latency-wise? maybe adds 10–20ms to cold handoffs.
dan: Which is lower-risk for an immediate canary rollback? We need something reversible and small.
ben: (B) is lower-risk for rollout. Add a field `session_origin`=transient|final and emit `reconcile=true` when resume reconciles. Billing pipeline can ignore transient starts if a final start follows within X ms and same resume-id.
carla: I can add a telemetry tag in the proxy: `x-routed-as=transient` for the initial accept. That would help the console show why we got the spike.
alice: Also need a console dashboard panel that highlights `starts_by_connect_method` split by `x-routed-as` and by `resume_id_present`. Right now dashboards only show raw starts and duplicates hide signal.
ben: I'll file a tiny billing-side parser tweak to treat transient+final with same resume-id as a single start if delta < 2s. Should be low-risk.
dan: And UX: add a canary annotation in console showing flagged sessions so SREs don't chase it. We can use `connect_method` + `x-routed-as` to flag.
carla: Patch I ran locally: proxy sets header on initial accept `X-Routed-As: transient` and router emits event `start_type=transient`. I can push a canary to staging.
ben: Deploy-bot: rolling canary to staging group [[deploy-bot]] :rocket:
deploy-bot: Rolling canary: env=staging, service=router, version=patch-transient-headers, 3/3 hosts updated.
infra-bot: Metric alert suppressed: AlertID #9123 suppressed for 1h (reason: suspected double-counting during canary).
alice: After we land billing dedupe and console panel, we should follow up with (A) router change to avoid emitting transient start when resume token already in-flight — but that's a medium-risk refactor.
ben: Timeline proposal: (1) immediate — emit `X-Routed-As: transient` and billing-side dedupe rule (today/next 24h). (2) short (week) — console panel + suppression annotation. (3) medium (2–3 wks) — router change to prefer resume validation before start event.
dan: Sounds good. Can we add a feature flag so product can toggle the dedupe behavior for sensitive enterprise accounts?
ben: Yes — billing dedupe rule will have `org_whitelist` config; default on for all internal staging, opt-in for customers until we validate.
carla: I'll open the PR with the header patch and add test logs. Also include a small note in the postmortem/rollout doc about telemetry keys we added.
alice: And I'll coordinate runtime tests to ensure resume latency doesn't regress more than 15ms on p50.
carla: Thanks. I'll post the PR link when ready. :thumbsup:
